purpose: prove that a third party can follow README.md from a fresh installation and reach doctor, the serve/request/status/report/replay chain, replay and report

steps.step: install from a fresh venv with the README command
steps.detail: the package and all dependencies resolved; pocket-harness.exe is on the fresh venv's Scripts path
starter configuration written; defaults point at http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1 and qwen2.5-coder:7b
5 of 6 checks pass; tools.round_trip fails because qwen2.5-coder:7b returned no structured tool call — exactly the documented capability profile (README: 0/3 probes); ok:false, exit 1
6 of 6 checks pass, ok:true; the tool-call round trip validated against the schema

steps.step: serve -> request -> status -> report -> replay with the fresh venv's CLI (scripts/e2e_cli_check.py with PH_E2E_PYTHON pointing at the fresh interpreter)
steps.detail: mock upstream; every command exited 0; the replay matched (input, config and output hashes equal, rules [])

steps.step: pytest tests -q and ruff check src tests scripts with the fresh venv's interpreter
steps.detail: 238 tests passed, ruff clean — the [dev] extras work

summary.honest_failure_demonstrated: the default model's tool round-trip failure is reported as a failure, not papered over
notes: the doctor run exercised the user's own Ollama 0.40.6 at 127.0.0.1:11434; no benchmark claims are derived from it
the state roots used were script-owned isolated directories; ~/.pocket was not touched
